verses.zh: 「若有人听见发誓的声音（或译：若有人听见叫人发誓的声音），他本是见证，却不把所看见的、所知道的说出来，这就是罪；他要担当他的罪孽。
verses.en: “‘When a person sins[NOTE:1] in that he hears a public curse against one who fails to testify[NOTE:2] and he is a witness (he either saw or knew what had happened[NOTE:3]) and he does not make it known,[NOTE:4] then he will bear his punishment for iniquity.[NOTE:5]
notes: The same expression occurs in Lev 4:2 where it introduces sins done “by straying unintentionally from any of the commandments of the Lord which must not be done” (see the notes there). Lev 5:1-13 is an additional section of sin offering regulations directed at violations other than those referred to by this expression in Lev 4:2 (see esp. 5:1-6), and expanding on the offering regulations for the common person in Lev 4:27-35 with concessions to the poor common person (5:7-13). tn Heb “And a person when he sins.” Most English versions translate this as the protasis of a conditional clause: “if a person sins” (NASB, NIV).

The words “against one who fails to testify” are not in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied to make sense of the remark about the “curse” (“imprecation” or “oath”; cf. ASV “adjuration”; NIV “public charge”) for the modern reader. For the interpretation of this verse reflected in the present translation see J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:292-97.
The words “what had happened” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied.
Heb “and hears a voice of curse, and he is a witness or he saw or he knew, if he does not declare.”

Heb “and he shall bear his iniquity.” The rendering “bear the punishment (for the iniquity)” reflects the use of the word “iniquity” to refer to the punishment for iniquity (cf. NRSV, NLT “subject to punishment”). It is sometimes referred to as the consequential use of the term (cf. Lev 5:17; 7:18; 10:17; etc.).

verses.zh: 或是有人摸了不洁的物，无论是不洁的死兽，是不洁的死畜，是不洁的死虫，他却不知道，因此成了不洁，就有了罪。
verses.en: Or when there is[NOTE:1] a person who touches anything ceremonially unclean,[NOTE:2] whether the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or the carcass of an unclean domesticated animal, or the carcass of an unclean creeping thing, even if he did not realize it,[NOTE:3] he has become unclean and is guilty;[NOTE:4]
notes: The insertion of the words “when there is” is a reflection of the few Hebrew mss, Smr, and LXX that have כִּי (ki, “when, if”; cf. vv. 3 and esp. 4) rather than the MT’s אֲשֶׁר (ʾasher, “who”). Many English versions render this as a conditional clause (“if”).
The word “ceremonially” has been supplied in the translation to clarify that the uncleanness involved is ritual or ceremonial in nature.

Heb “and it is hidden from him,” meaning that the person who contracted the ceremonial uncleanness was not aware at the time what had happened, but later found out that he had become ceremonially unclean. This same phrase occurs again in both vv. 3 and 4.

Lev 5:2-3 are parallel laws of uncleanness (contracted from animals and people, respectively), and both seem to assume that the contraction of uncleanness was originally unknown to the person (vv. 2 and 3) but became known to him or her at a later time (v. 3; i.e., “has come to know” in v. 3 is to be assumed for v. 2 as well). Uncleanness itself did not make a person “guilty” unless he or she failed to handle it according to the normal purification regulations (see, e.g., “wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening,” Lev 15:5 NIV11; cf. Lev 11:39-40; 15:5-12, 16-24; Num 19, etc.). The problem here in Lev 5:2-3 is that, because the person had not been aware of his or her uncleanness, he or she had incurred guilt for not carrying out these regular procedures, and it would now be too late for that. Thus, the unclean person needs to bring a sin offering to atone for the contamination caused by his or her neglect of the purity regulations.

verses.zh: 或是他摸了别人的污秽，无论是染了甚么污秽，他却不知道，一知道了就有了罪。
verses.en: or when he touches human uncleanness with regard to anything by which he can become unclean,[NOTE:1] even if he did not realize it, but he has later come to know it and is guilty;
notes: Heb “or if he touches uncleanness of mankind to any of his uncleanness which he becomes unclean in it.”

verses.zh: 或是有人嘴里冒失发誓，要行恶，要行善，无论人在甚么事上冒失发誓，他却不知道，一知道了就要在这其中的一件上有了罪。
verses.en: or when a person swears an oath, speaking thoughtlessly[NOTE:1] with his lips, whether to do evil or to do good, with regard to anything which the individual might speak thoughtlessly in an oath, even if he did not realize it, but he has later come to know it and is guilty with regard to one of these oaths[NOTE:2]—
notes: Heb “to speak thoughtlessly”; cf. NAB “rashly utters an oath.”

Heb “and is guilty to one from these,” probably referring here to any of “these” things about which one might swear a thoughtless oath (J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 45), with the word “oath” supplied in the translation for clarity. Another possibility is that “to one from these” is a dittography from v. 5 (cf. the note on v. 5a), and that v. 4 ends with “and is guilty” like vv. 2 and 3 (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:300).

verses.zh: 他有了罪的时候，就要承认所犯的罪，
verses.en: when an individual becomes guilty with regard to one of these things[NOTE:1] he must confess how he has sinned,[NOTE:2]
notes: What all the transgressions in Lev 5:1-4 have in common is that the time is past for handling the original situation properly (i.e., testifying in court, following purity regulations, or fulfilling an oath), so now the person has become guilty and needs to follow corrective sacrificial procedures. tn Heb “and it shall happen when he becomes guilty to one from these,” referring to any of “these” possible transgressions in Lev 5:1-4. The Cairo Geniza Hb ms, the LXX, and the Latin Vulgate omit this clause, possibly due to homoioteleuton because of the repetition of “to one from these” from the end of v. 4 in v. 5a (cf. the note on v. 4b).
Heb “which he sinned on it”; cf. ASV “confess that wherein he hath sinned”; NCV “must tell how he sinned.”

verses.zh: 并要因所犯的罪，把他的赎愆祭牲―就是羊群中的母羊，或是一只羊羔，或是一只山羊―牵到耶和华面前为赎罪祭。至于他的罪，祭司要为他赎了。
verses.en: and he must bring his penalty for guilt[NOTE:1] to the Lord for his sin that he has committed—a female from the flock, whether a female sheep or a female goat, for a sin offering. So the priest will make atonement[NOTE:2] on his behalf for[NOTE:3] his sin.
notes: In this context the word for “guilt” (אָשָׁם, ʾasham) refers to the “penalty” for incurring guilt, the so-called consequential אָשָׁם (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:303; cf. the note on Lev 5:1).
The focus of sin offering “atonement” was purging impurities from the tabernacle (see the note on Lev 1:4).
See the note on 4:26 regarding the use of מִן (min).

verses.zh: 「他的力量若不够献一只羊羔，就要因所犯的罪，把两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽带到耶和华面前为赎愆祭：一只作赎罪祭，一只作燔祭。
verses.en: “‘If he cannot afford an animal from the flock,[NOTE:1] he must bring his penalty for guilt for his sin that he has committed,[NOTE:2] two turtledoves or two young pigeons,[NOTE:3] to the Lord, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
notes: Heb “and if his hand does not reach enough of a flock animal” (see the note on v. 11 below). The term translated “animal from the flock” (שֶׂה, seh) is often translated “lamb” (e.g., KJV, NASB, NIV, NCV) or “sheep” (e.g., NRSV, TEV, NLT), but it clearly includes either a sheep or a goat here (cf. v. 6), referring to the smaller pasture animals as opposed to the larger ones (i.e., cattle; cf. 4:3). Some English versions use the more generic “animal” (e.g., NAB, CEV).

Heb “and he shall bring his guilt which he sinned,” which is an abbreviated form of Lev 5:6, “and he shall bring his [penalty for] guilt to the Lord for his sin which he committed.” The words “for his sin” have been left out in v. 7, and “to the Lord” has been moved so that it follows the mention of the birds.
See the note on Lev 1:14 above.

verses.zh: 把这些带到祭司那里，祭司就要先把那赎罪祭献上，从鸟的颈项上揪下头来，只是不可把鸟撕断，
verses.en: He must bring them to the priest and present first the one that is for a sin offering. The priest[NOTE:1] must pinch[NOTE:2] its head at the nape of its neck, but must not sever the head from the body.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he.” The subject (“he”) refers to the priest here, not the offerer who presented the birds to the priest (cf. v. 8a).

The action seems to involve both a twisting action, breaking the neck of the bird and severing its vertebrae, as well as pinching or nipping the skin, but in this case not severing the head from the main body (note the rest of this verse).
Heb “he shall not divide [it]” (see J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:305).

verses.zh: 也把些赎罪祭牲的血弹在坛的旁边，剩下的血要流在坛的脚那里；这是赎罪祭。
verses.en: Then he must sprinkle[NOTE:1] some of the blood of the sin offering on the wall of the altar, and the remainder of the blood[NOTE:2] must be squeezed out at the base of the altar—it is a sin offering.
notes: The Hebrew verb וְהִזָּה (vehizzah, Hiphil of נָזָה, nazah) does indeed mean “sprinkle” or “splatter” (cf. Lev 4:6, 17). Contrast “splash” in Lev 1:5, etc. (זָרָק, zaraq).
Heb “the remainder in the blood.” The preposition ב (bet, “in”) is used here to mean “some among” a whole collection of something.

verses.zh: 他要照例献第二只为燔祭。至于他所犯的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。
verses.en: The second bird[NOTE:1] he must make a burnt offering according to the standard regulation.[NOTE:2] So the priest will make atonement[NOTE:3] on behalf of this person for[NOTE:4] his sin which he has committed, and he will be forgiven.[NOTE:5]
notes: The word “bird” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation for clarity.
The term “[standard] regulation” (מִשְׁפָּט, mishpat) here refers to the set of regulations for burnt offering birds in Lev 1:14-17.
The focus of sin offering “atonement” was purging impurities from the tabernacle (see the note on Lev 1:4).
See the note on 4:26 with regard to מִן, min.
Heb “there shall be forgiveness to him” or “it shall be forgiven to him” (KJV similar).

verses.zh: 「他的力量若不够献两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，就要因所犯的罪带供物来，就是细面伊法十分之一为赎罪祭；不可加上油，也不可加上乳香，因为是赎罪祭。
verses.en: “‘If he cannot afford[NOTE:1] two turtledoves or two young pigeons,[NOTE:2] he must bring as his offering for his sin which he has committed[NOTE:3] a tenth of an ephah[NOTE:4] of choice wheat flour[NOTE:5] for a sin offering. He must not place olive oil on it, and he must not put frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
notes: Heb “and if his hand does not reach [or is not sufficient] to”; cf. NASB “if his means are insufficient for.” The expression is the same as that in Lev 5:7 above except for the verb: נָשַׂג (nasag, “to collect, to reach, to be sufficient”) is used here, but נָגַע (nagah, “to touch, to reach”) is used in v. 7. Smr has the former in both v. 7 and 11.
See the note on Lev 1:14 above (cf. also 5:7).

Heb “and he shall bring his offering which he sinned.” Like the similar expression in v. 7 above (see the note there), this is an abbreviated form of Lev 5:6, “and he shall bring his [penalty for] guilt to the Lord for his sin which he committed.” Here the words “to the Lord for his sin” have been left out, and “his [penalty for] guilt” has been changed to “his offering.”

A tenth of an ephah would be about 2.3 liters, one day’s ration for a single person (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:306). English versions handle the amount somewhat differently, cf. NCV “about two quarts”; TEV “one kilogramme”; CEV “two pounds.”
See the note on Lev 2:1 above.

verses.zh: 他要把供物带到祭司那里，祭司要取出自己的一把来作为纪念，按献给耶和华火祭的条例烧在坛上；这是赎罪祭。
verses.en: He must bring it to the priest, and the priest must scoop out from it a handful as its memorial portion[NOTE:1] and offer it up in smoke on the altar on top of the other gifts of the Lord—it is a sin offering.
notes: The “memorial portion” (אַזְכָּרָה, ʾazkarah) was the part of the grain offering that was burnt on the altar (Lev 2:2), as opposed to the remainder, which was normally consumed by the priests (Lev 2:3; see the full regulations in Lev 6:14-23 [6:7-16 HT]). It was probably intended to call to mind (i.e., memorialize) before the Lord the reason for the presentation of the particular offering (see the remarks in R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 1:335-39).

verses.zh: 至于他在这几件事中所犯的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。剩下的面都归与祭司，和素祭一样。」
verses.en: So the priest will make atonement[NOTE:1] on his behalf for his sin which he has committed by doing one of these things,[NOTE:2] and he will be forgiven.[NOTE:3] The remainder of the offering[NOTE:4] will belong to the priest like the grain offering.’”[NOTE:5]
notes: The focus of sin offering “atonement” was purging impurities from the tabernacle (see the note on Lev 1:4).
Heb “from one from these,” referring to the four kinds of violations of the law delineated in Lev 5:1-4 (see the note on Lev 5:5 above and cf. Lev 4:27).
Heb “there shall be forgiveness to him” or “it shall be forgiven to him” (KJV similar).
Heb “and it”; the referent (the remaining portion of the offering) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and it shall be to the priest like the grain offering,” referring to the rest of the grain that was not offered on the altar (cf. the regulations in Lev 2:3, 10).

verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:[NOTE:1]
notes: The quotation introduced here extends from Lev 5:14 through 5:19, encompassing the first main section of guilt offering regulations. Compare the notes on Lev 1:1; 4:1; and 6:1 [5:20 HT].

verses.zh: 「人若在耶和华的圣物上误犯了罪，有了过犯，就要照你所估的，按圣所的舍客勒拿银子，将赎愆祭牲―就是羊群中一只没有残疾的公绵羊―牵到耶和华面前为赎愆祭；
verses.en: “When a person commits a trespass[NOTE:1] and sins by straying unintentionally[NOTE:2] from the regulations about the Lord’s holy things,[NOTE:3] then he must bring his penalty for guilt[NOTE:4] to the Lord, a flawless ram from the flock, convertible into silver shekels according to the standard of the sanctuary shekel,[NOTE:5] for a guilt offering.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “trespasses a trespass” (verb and direct object from the same Hebrew root, מַעַל, maʿal); cf. NIV84 “commits a violation.” The word refers to some kind of overstepping of the boundary between that which is common (i.e., available for common use by common people) and that which is holy (i.e., to be used only for holy purposes because it has been consecrated to the Lord, see further below). See the note on Lev 10:10.
See Lev 4:2 above for a note on “straying.”

Heb “from the holy things of the Lord.” The Hebrew expression here has the same structure as Lev 4:2, “from any of the commandments of the Lord.” The latter introduces the sin offering regulations and the former the guilt offering regulations. The sin offering deals with violations of “any of the commandments,” whereas the guilt offering focuses specifically on violations of regulations regarding “holy things” (i.e., things that have been consecrated to the Lord; see the full discussion in J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:320-27).
Here the word for “guilt” (אָשָׁם, ʾasham) refers to the “penalty” for incurring guilt, the so-called consequential use of אָשָׁם (ʾasham; see J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:303).

The sanctuary shekel was about 10 grams (= ca. two-fifths of an ounce; J. E. Shepherd, NIDOTTE 4:237-38).tn Heb “in your valuation, silver of shekels, in the shekel of the sanctuary.” The translation offered here suggests that, instead of a ram, the guilt offering could be presented in the form of money (see, e.g., NRSV; J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:326-27). Others still maintain the view that it refers to the value of the ram that was offered (see, e.g., NIV “of the proper value in silver, according to the sanctuary shekel”; also NAB, NLT; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 72-73, 81).

The word for “guilt offering” (sometimes translated “reparation offering”) is the same as “guilt” earlier in the verse (rendered there “[penalty for] guilt”). One can tell which is intended only by the context.sn The primary purpose of the guilt offering was to “atone” (see the note on Lev 1:4 above) for “trespassing” on the Lord’s “holy things” (see later in this verse) or the property of others in the community (Lev 6:1-7 [5:20-26 HT]; 19:20-22; Num 5:5-10). It was closely associated with reconsecration of the Lord’s sacred things or his sacred people (see, e.g., Lev 14:12-18; Num 6:11b-12). Moreover, there was usually an associated reparation made for the trespass, including restitution of that which was violated plus one-fifth of its value as a fine (Lev 5:16; 6:5 [5:24 HT]). See R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 1:557-66.

verses.zh: 并且他因在圣物上的差错要偿还，另外加五分之一，都给祭司。祭司要用赎愆祭的公绵羊为他赎罪，他必蒙赦免。
verses.en: And whatever holy thing he violated[NOTE:1] he must restore and must add one-fifth to it and give it to the priest. So the priest will make atonement[NOTE:2] on his behalf with the guilt-offering ram, and he will be forgiven.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and which he sinned from the holy thing.”
Regarding “make atonement” see the note on Lev 1:4.
Heb “there shall be forgiveness to him” or “it shall be forgiven to him” (KJV similar).

verses.zh: 「若有人犯罪，行了耶和华所吩咐不可行的甚么事，他虽然不知道，还是有了罪，就要担当他的罪孽；
verses.en: “If a person sins and violates any of the Lord’s commandments that must not be violated[NOTE:1] (although he did not know it at the time,[NOTE:2] but later realizes he is guilty), then he will bear his punishment for iniquity[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and does one from all of the commandments of the Lord that must not be done.”
The words “at the time” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied.

Heb “and he did not know, and he shall be guilty and he shall bear his iniquity” (for the rendering “bear his punishment [for iniquity]”) see the note on Lev 5:1.) This portion of v. 17 is especially difficult. The translation offered here suggests (as in many other English versions) that the offender did not originally know that he had violated the Lord’s commandments, but then came to know it and dealt with it accordingly (cf. the corresponding sin offering section in Lev 5:1-4). Another possibility is that it refers to a situation where a person suspects that he violated something although he does not recollect it. Thus, he brings a guilt offering for his suspected violation (J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:331-34, 361-63). See also R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 1:561-62.

verses.zh: 也要照你所估定的价，从羊群中牵一只没有残疾的公绵羊来，给祭司作赎愆祭。至于他误行的那错事，祭司要为他赎罪，他必蒙赦免。
verses.en: and must bring a flawless ram from the flock, convertible into silver shekels,[NOTE:1] for a guilt offering to the priest. So the priest will make atonement[NOTE:2] on his behalf for his error that he committed[NOTE:3] (although he himself had not known it), and he will be forgiven.[NOTE:4]
notes: The statement here is condensed. See the full expression in 5:15 and the note there.
Regarding “make atonement” see the note on Lev 1:4.
Heb “on his straying which he strayed.” See the note on Lev 4:2.
Heb “there shall be forgiveness to him” or “it shall be forgiven to him” (KJV and NASB both similar).

verses.zh: 这是赎愆祭，因他在耶和华面前实在有了罪。」
verses.en: It is a guilt offering; he was surely guilty before the Lord.”
